# generator-shortcuts — 4ecf2a93671f

> For this generator, name the strongest plausible shortcut or rival rule that
> fits the canonical demonstrations. Give an exact input on which it disagrees
> with the intended rule, how you checked the output, and whether your proposed
> generator emits such cases.

## Rival that actually fits the canonical data

`fixed_side3_output` is the strongest retained canonical-fitting shortcut:
perform the zero-mask self-product on 3×3 inputs, but always return a 9×9 output.
Its declared implementation truncates a larger rule-mirror result to the first
nine rows and columns. All four canonical labeled pairs have 3×3 inputs and
9×9 outputs, so this rival fits every canonical demonstration and the canonical
test. That 4/4 fit is checked from the actual declaration and retained in the
source-bound census; it is not an assumption based only on input dimensions.

The other five named rivals are useful semantic mistakes but are not claimed to
fit every canonical pair. They test block-only, subcell-only, OR, foreground
self-product and count-only predictions.

## Exact generated counterexample

Input: **4 rows × 4 columns**. Output: **16 rows × 16 columns**.

```json
[[9,9,9,0],
 [9,0,0,9],
 [0,9,9,9],
 [9,9,9,9]]
```

Recipe: seed `10982922816027`, sample index `3262`, difficulty `easy`, no overrides,
generator v3.1.0, SHA-256
`edf751b6db95b382517a9f5434229c7b7fa0aff0740f6129235ba100831a49de`.
The input passes the selected self-check and lies inside ordinary generated
support: side 4, paint 9, four zero cells.

The selected Racket authority returns **16 rows × 16 columns**, with 16 painted
cells. Using zero-based coordinates, the input zero support is
Z = {(0,3), (1,1), (1,2), (2,0)}. Every pair of zero coordinates contributes
paint at `(4*r1+r2, 4*c1+c2)`. For example, output `(0,15)` is 9.
The rival returns only **9 rows × 9 columns** and has no cell at `(0,15)`.
Full exact authority and rival outputs are retained in
`repo/generators/4ecf2a93671f/counterexamples/fixed_side3_output.json`.

## How the output was checked

This is an actual retained semantic-gate witness, not a Python-mirror-only label.
The final battery executed the selected Racket rule, checked the input, and
compared the rival prediction. The witness binds generator bytes, exact Racket
source SHA-256 `53f92782daaab4b77c75e30ba01bbc8750b63da071968f891328202d10bfc1aa`
and executable callable hash. Its source report is
`checks/after-final/checks/4ecf2a93671f_after_semantic_gate.json`, at
`audits[0].witnesses.output_size_scales_with_input.rival_claim.witness_examples.fixed_side3_output`.

The final outer command was:

```bash
WORK/.venv-review/bin/python review.py check --battery --compact-results \
  --phase after --timeout 4000 --schedule-census ../checks/schedule-census.json \
  --require-rotations-identifiable --out ../checks/after-final
```

Its working directory was the outer extraction directory; the wrapper executed
the payload from WORK/repo. Exact absolute invocation and exit 0 are recorded
in RESULTS.json. The independent input-replay receipt is
`checks/counterexample-replay.json`.

## Does the proposed distribution teach this distinction?

Yes. The ordinary size schedule is 3,3,4,5, so larger-size cases occupy half
the schedule and each three-consecutive-demo window contains one. The semantic
census measured 288/600 larger-size witnesses, with 60/60 retained oracle/rival
checks disagreeing. These are measured random counts, distinct from the exact
two-of-four schedule proportion. The witness itself is a default generated case.

At the lesson level, 300 production lessons and all 1,200 query rotations were
clean against the six declared rivals. The additional fixed-seed enumeration
covered 36 lessons and 144 rotations across all 12 schedule starts and three
bands. These results support this specific schedule and rival family; they do
not establish uniqueness among every imaginable rule or every override policy.

The repaired hook also handles the converse honestly: if all demonstrations and
the actual query are canonical-size, this rival cannot change the query answer
and is not a reason to reject the lesson. The same demos with a larger query
are rejected until the size distinction has been demonstrated.
